description: We are the Space Mangoes, a team of Computer Science students interested in using technology to solve real-world problems related to space and Earth science. We love mangoes.
summary:
Hubas is a web app that helps people explore how water changed during the 2026 wet season in Cebu and Bohol. It follows three things: soil water in 101 towns and cities, water area at Malinao Dam, and radar signals from two rice parcels. People can view maps, images, charts, dates, and even hear the data as sound.

Our project answers the “Dancing with the SARs” challenge by making satellite radar data easier to explore and understand. The app also shows where data is missing and explains what the readings can and cannot tell us. This matters because local offices, water districts, teachers, and the public can use the information as a starting point for questions or field checks. Hubas does not predict drought or explain the cause of every change.
details:
Hubas is a website built with Next.js and TypeScript. It uses MapLibre for the map and Web Audio to play sounds linked to the data. A Python pipeline prepares the NASA satellite data and saves it as files the app can use. The app does not call NASA services while someone is using it.

Visitors can move through dates, choose a town, compare radar images, and view changes in charts. The Score page puts soil, dam, rice, and rain data on one timeline. Users can turn on different sound parts to hear the data.

We used NISAR data for soil water and radar images, Sentinel-1 data for past dam changes, GPM for rain, and SMAP to check the soil water pattern. We also explain that some soil readings are provisional, coverage changes, and radar alone cannot confirm crop growth or the cause of a change. Our goal is to help people explore the evidence and decide what they may want to check next.
